skill.description: Provides Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS/Fargate patterns for containerized application deployment.
skill.summary: Guides container deployment patterns across Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS/Fargate.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, localhost health checks, apt cleanup, and legitimate container user setup. Confirmed issues are insecure copy-paste patterns: weak default database credentials, hardcoded dummy secrets, a debug listener on all interfaces, and broad Kubernetes secret access. No prompt injection attempt or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Weak or hardcoded secret examples appear in Compose and Kubernetes templates.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sample credentials with placeholders and require runtime secret managers or local environment files outside version control.

remediation.issue: A debug container example listens on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Bind debug tooling to loopback where possible and mark debug targets as isolated, temporary, and not for production.

remediation.issue: The Kubernetes RBAC example can list all secrets in the namespace.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the list verb for secrets and restrict access with resourceNames when a workload needs one specific secret.

remediation.issue: Build and deployment commands can affect registries and clusters when run in the wrong context.
remediation.suggestion: Add preflight checks that print the Docker registry, Kubernetes context, AWS account, and target namespace before mutating commands.

semantic_findings.title: Over-Permissive Kubernetes Secret Access
semantic_findings.description: The Kubernetes RBAC example grants the application role get and list access to secrets. Production workloads should avoid broad secret listing and should scope access to specific secret names where possible.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Role explicitly includes resources configmaps and secrets with get and list verbs. This is a clear least-privilege issue in a production manifest example.

content.value_statement: Container deployment work often needs repeatable Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS patterns. This skill provides templates, examples, and operational guidance for common orchestration tasks.
actual_capabilities: Provides Dockerfile patterns for multi-stage builds, non-root users, health checks, and image labels.
Includes a Docker Compose starter template with app, database, Redis, health checks, networks, and volumes.
Shows Kubernetes manifests for deployments, services, ingress, autoscaling, pod disruption budgets, RBAC, and network policies.
Documents Helm chart structure, values files, helper templates, deployment templates, and common Helm commands.
Explains AWS ECS on Fargate concepts, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, observability, and deployment tooling.
Includes a Bash script for building Docker images and optionally pushing them to a configured registry.
limitations: Examples require review before production use, especially secrets, ports, registry names, and access policies.
The skill does not validate manifests against a live cluster, registry, or AWS account.
The build script requires Docker, local shell access, and registry credentials when pushing images.
Platform details can change, so AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, and Helm versions must be checked.

use_cases.title: Create Deployment Starters
use_cases.description: Generate an initial Dockerfile, Compose file, or Kubernetes manifest set for a new service.

use_cases.title: Review Container Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare a service configuration against common production patterns for users, probes, resources, and rollout safety.

use_cases.title: Plan AWS Fargate Services
use_cases.description: Map an application to ECS tasks, services, IAM roles, networking, secrets, scaling, and observability choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Container Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single web service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Dockerfile and Docker Compose plan for my web service. Include health checks, a non-root user, and local development notes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to Kubernetes Manifests
prompt_templates.scenario: Move a containerized service into Kubernetes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this service description into Kubernetes manifests. Include deployment, service, ingress, resources, probes, secrets references, and rollout settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Helm Chart
prompt_templates.scenario: Package a service for repeatable Kubernetes installs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Helm chart structure for this application. Include values files, helper templates, security settings, autoscaling, and environment overrides.

prompt_templates.title: Compare ECS and Kubernetes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced platform decision for production deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECS on Fargate and Kubernetes for this workload. Cover networking, IAM, secrets, scaling, observability, cost, and operational tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A Python API needs a production container setup.
output: A multi-stage image plan with dependency caching and a non-root runtime user.
Health check and exposed port guidance for the application.
Notes about secrets, environment variables, and files that should stay outside the image.

output_examples.input: A team wants to deploy one service to Kubernetes.
output: A manifest checklist covering namespace, deployment, service, ingress, probes, resource limits, and autoscaling.
Recommendations for secret references, network policy, and pod disruption protection.
Operational notes for rollout checks and troubleshooting commands.

output_examples.input: An AWS team is choosing between ECS Fargate and Kubernetes.
output: A decision summary based on portability, operational burden, networking, IAM integration, and ecosystem needs.
A Fargate service plan covering task roles, execution roles, subnets, load balancing, logging, and scaling.
Risks to verify before production, including secrets access and private network routing.

best_practices: Review all generated templates before use and replace sample values with environment-specific settings.
Use runtime secret managers or Kubernetes secret references instead of baking secrets into images or manifests.
Run security and policy checks on Dockerfiles, Helm output, and Kubernetes manifests before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample passwords, API keys, or database URLs into production environments.
Do not expose debug listeners, databases, or cache services unless access is tightly controlled.
Do not run build, push, kubectl, Helm, or AWS commands without checking the current context and target account.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy containers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, templates, and commands that a user must review and run intentionally.

faq.question: Can it help with Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a starter Compose template with an app service, database, Redis, health checks, networks, and volumes.

faq.question: Can it generate Kubernetes resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common manifests such as deployments, services, ingress, autoscaling, RBAC, and network policies.

faq.question: Does it support Helm?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents chart layout, values files, helpers, deployment templates, and common Helm commands.

faq.question: Does it cover AWS ECS on Fargate?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains task definitions, services, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, logs, and deployment tooling.

faq.question: What should users review most carefully?
faq.answer: Users should review secrets, exposed ports, cluster context, registry targets, IAM permissions, and production environment settings.
